Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) suffered a medial ankle sprain in the Week 3 game against the Denver Broncos , and he appears likely to miss the Week 4 game against the Philadelphia Eagles , head coach Sean McVay said Monday, Sept. 28.

Why it Matters: The Rams dressed five tight ends for Sunday Night Football in Denver due to a shortage at wide receiver, so they have plenty of other options at the position. Veteran Tyler Higbee shined with eight receptions for 62 yards and a score, while Davis Allen and Colby Parkinson are also options. The latter suffered a shoulder injury, but it appears to be minor. Higbee is likely the best bet from a fantasy perspective, however.

articles.title: Manchester City's Premier League charges: What comes next?
articles.summary: Manchester City's fate in a legal battle with the Premier League is yet to be sealed, but reports they have been found guilty on widespread financial miscond...
articles.body:
Manchester City 's fate in a legal battle with the Premier League is yet to be sealed, but reports they have been found guilty on widespread financial misconduct has sparked speculation of what comes next.

The dominant Premier League force for more than a decade, swingeing sanctions against City would send shockwaves through English football.

Rival clubs are set to launch their own legal action seeking hundreds of millions of pounds in compensation, while there is debate over whether some of City's many titles and trophies over the past 15 years could be stripped.

AFP Sports looks at the next steps and potential fall out from the case:

The Athletic first reported on Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they faced.

However, no sanction has yet been approved.

Even once a decision is made on how City will be punished, should they be found guilty, the club are almost certain to appeal.

In a letter to City fans on Saturday, the club's chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said: "Our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

A case that began after German outlet Der Spiegel published leaked documents from City executives in 2018, could still take a lengthy time to fully resolve.

According to Premier League rules, the sanction can vary from a points deduction, a fine or even expulsion from the division.

Everton and Nottingham Forest were handed points deductions in the 2023/24 season for single breaches of financial sustainability rules. On that basis, City would face almost certain relegation if found guilty of over 100 charges.

Whether the sanction is applied before an appeal is heard will be another bone of contention.

If it is, City could face relegation before overturning any guilty verdict.

On the other hand, if City, who currently sit top of the table, are not punished until after an appeal, it could cost other clubs their place in the top-flight or lucrative European qualification.

Even after the Premier League process if over, there is also the chance that City's Abu-Dhabi backed owners seek redress in England's High Court if they challenge a legal issue regarding how the arbitration process was conducted.

City's rivals were quick to revel in the news of their potential demise.

"Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet," posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand , who was part of the United team to finish second to City in the 2011/12 season.

The reality is that stripping and retroactively awarding titles is a messy process.

City's charges relate to the period between 2009 and 2018. In that time they won four league titles, with United and Liverpool twice finishing second in those seasons.

Yet City have won another four since, arguably built on foundations that were fraudulently gained.

They also won four League Cups and one FA Cup, the club's first trophy for 35 years, in the period between 2009 and 2018.

"I don't seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either," Tony Pulis, whose Stoke side lost the 2011 FA Cup final to City, told the BBC.

"A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely. But I still feel cheated."

A more likely source of recompense for clubs that missed out is through financial compensation.

In June, Everton were told they must pay Burnley £35 million ($46 million) after they edged out the Clarets to Premier League survival in the same season they broke financial sustainability rules.

Less than a month ago, City completed the biggest ever transfer spend in one window, splashing out around £460 million on the likes of Enzo Fernandez , Elliott Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi .

The impending verdict on the charges has to this point made little impact on City's ability to attract and retain their star names.

Talismanic striker Erling Haaland signed a nine-year contract in 2025 that could keep him tied down till his 34th birthday.

How many, if any, of the players managed to negotiate exit clauses in the case City were heavily sanctioned remains to be seen.

articles.title: Will the College Football Playoff selection committee's new rules make their rankings better?
articles.summary: The College Football Playoff committee is adding strength of conference as a new metric, but questions about transparency and bias remain unanswered.
articles.body: There's no question that the College Football Playoff selection committee has a difficult job. And one where it's virtually impossible to please all interested parties. In the current format, just 12 college football teams reach the playoffs, which has become the ultimate sign of success or failure for a program's season. Coaching changes are decided based on playoff appearances. Conference bragging rights, both in the public discourse and in deliberations, are determined based on playoff appearances. Given the competing priorities at play, there's little chance of keeping everyone happy. There will always be a 13th best team in the country. Or a Power 4 school that feels like they missed out to allow a Group of 6 school to reach the tournament. Conferences will advocate for more of their member teams to be included. Group of 6 schools will argue that they deserve to be included after a good season, even if their schedules can't match up to top teams. FLORIDA GATORS, MISSISSIPPI STATE SOAR, USC TUMBLES IN LATEST INEXPLICABLE AP TOP 25 POLL It's a guarantee that their choices will lead to disagreement, debate, and some level of unhappiness. Especially because the rankings are based on human evaluation, and humans make mistakes, are biased, or have their own individual priorities and valuations. Which is what makes the opacity of the committee's process and evaluation tools so frustrating. For years, committee members have spoken about how they incorporate strength of schedule and resume into their deliberations and their top 25 poll. But there's little transparency as to how they determine the strength of schedule and resume. It's nice to say it, it's another to show your work. Are they creating their own metrics based on wins and losses against, say, AP ranked teams? Or is it just eye test? Or do they use more advanced, computer-driven analytics? Who knows? Well, the committee revealed recently that they're now adding another metric to help inform their discussions: strength of conference. Oh good, more metrics with little transparency that will lead to more debate and disagreement. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Heather Dinich from ESPN reported that the committee would now incorporate this new metric to help separate teams within the league. "The CFP selection committee will incorporate another data point in late November that helps determine the strength of each conference based on the schedule strength of each team in its league,' she posted on X. "It will help separate teams in the SAME LEAGUE with similar records based on the strength of their conference opponents. (Ex: PSU doesn’t play Oregon, Ohio State or IU) It will also help separate teams with comparable records in different conferences based on how tough their league opponents were." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Sure. Sounds reasonable enough. But what's it based on? How are they evaluating which teams have faced the "strongest" conference opponents? Win-loss record? AP Top 25 poll appearances? Random eye test? Computer analytics? How do they determine how to separate teams with comparable records in different conferences? Again, the questions that the committee wants answers to, evaluating different schedules and conferences, are all valuable and important debates. The issue is that there's no transparency on how they're going to do it. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Some fans look at wins and losses or head-to-head matchups. Some like to use "ranked wins" or ranked games, though those can often be misleading based on when those games happen. For example, Texas A&M counts as a ranked win for LSU, even though it's clear the Aggies are far from a top 25 team. Others like to use analytics-based systems that are more objective and less biased toward a specific school or conference. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD That should be the preference; remove bias, evaluate teams objectively, combine metrics to find the "best" teams that fit the criteria and limit the amount of campaigning and importance of the typically awful AP Poll. That should be the goal. But will it be the outcome? We'll find out in a few months. Then spend the months after arguing about it.

articles.title: Pablo Sala: "Yo creo que todos los equipos de Primera utilizan la inteligencia artificial"
articles.standfirst: El experto en la materia atiende a MARCA para explicar sus usos en el fútbol
articles.summary: El experto en la materia atiende a MARCA para explicar sus usos en el fútbol
articles.body: Pablo Sala atiende a MARCA tras posicionarse como un pionero en el uso de inteligencias artificiales aplicadas a la gestión de clubes deportivos, federaciones y academias, tanto en fútbol como en futsal. Pregunta: A alguien que no conozca el uso de la IA, ¿cómo le explicaría que funciona realmente en un club de fútbol o futsal? Respuesta: Hoy en día todo el mundo utiliza el CHATGPT de una forma más casera o profesional, entonces lo que intentamos hacer es utilizar el propio ChatGPT u otra herramienta de IA de forma profesional para que el club funcione de la mejor manera, una gestión más optimizada. Al final es utilizar bien las herramientas. P: ¿Cuál es la tarea que cree que es más común para que un club use la IA y ahorre tiempo y dinero? R: La más común hoy en los clubes no es la que más tiempo y dinero ahorra. Suele ser las de escribir: notas de prensa o emails para el ayuntamiento. Cosas muy básicas, la que más tiempo y dinero ahorra es la creación de aplicaciones. Puedes crearte una pequeña aplicación que te solucione una tarea de tu día a día y ahorrar muchas horas o dinero de no tener que pagar cierta aplicación que ya estás pagando. P: ¿En qué áreas de un club cree que tiene más potencial utilizar la IA? ¿Scouting, análisis de partidos, entrenamiento, comunicación...? R: Hay una parte deportiva de análisis de datos que nos ayuda mucho y también, a nivel de gestión en todo lo que es la burocracia, el papeleo. En lugar de leerte un PDF de 200 páginas de una subvención, te saca en dos minutos lo que tienes que presentar, cuánto es la cuantía, cuánto hay que justificarlo y que no se te pase nada. Eso es realmente lo que hoy te puede aportar más. Hay miles de ejemplos y, por ejemplo, en marketing estoy seguro de que ahora mismo desde la nota de prensa, el cartel del partido, un vídeo promocional, la web del campus, especialmente marketing y comunicación, una de las que más. P: ¿Hasta qué punto considera que, por ejemplo, las IA pueden ayudar a clubes más pequeños a acercarse a clubes que sean más grandes? R: A los clubes pequeños lo que les falta es orden, con lo cual, teniendo un objetivo claro, la IA te puede ayudar a ordenar muchos procesos. Los clubes grandes, que funcionan ya de una forma más profesional, también les puede ayudar, pero al final ya es mejorar lo que tienen. A un club pequeño le puede organizar completamente y eso es como pasar del cero al noventa en muy poco tiempo. P: Has trabajado también con clubes de fútbol sala. ¿La IA en qué cree que ayuda a este deporte? R: El fútbol sala, incluso los clubes de Primera División cuentan con recursos muy limitados en cuanto al personal, con lo cual, si tú en un club donde tienes tres personas ahora haces el trabajo de seis o incluso diez personas, evidentemente eso te va a dar un nivel mayor de tus contenidos y de tu preparación. P: ¿Hasta qué punto puede una IA ayudar a un entrenador a preparar un partido contra un rival concreto? R: Hay un aspecto táctico que, bajo el criterio del entrenador, se puede estudiar, pero hay quizá tareas en las que se analizan los resultados históricos. Ese nivel de búsquedas ya no hace falta que lo hagas, te lo hace concretamente la IA. También puedes buscar si ha habido lesiones. También depende del nivel de información que tengas. Puede ser desde la preparación física hasta la producción psicológica, tú puedes pedirle a ChatGPT que actúe como un psicólogo, siempre bajo la supervisión de un profesional o un preparador físico que te ayude a interpretar los 6.000 parámetros que da el típico GPS que se ponen los jugadores. Entonces, los equipos están utilizando una ínfima parte de esos datos para mejorar el rendimiento. Si la IA es capaz de encontrar patrones y de unificar criterios o este parámetro junto con otro puede funcionar muy bien y parece que es un indicador de rendimiento. P: ¿Cuál cree que es el límite entre ayudar a un entrenador o que condicione demasiado ya esas decisiones, la propia inteligencia artificial? R: Eso lo decide cada persona. Tú puedes delegarle tu criterio a la IA y entonces estás perdiendo tu decisión, o puedes apoyarte en ella para ciertas cosas. Cuanto más criterio tengas, más va a multiplicar. Si tú eres un entrenador de 5, pues va a ser de 10. Si tú eres un entrenador de 9, pues va a ser 18, con lo cual multiplica tus capacidades. A más criterio, más experiencia y más conocimiento tengas tú, mayor multiplicador es la IA. P: Bajo su experiencia, ¿cuáles son los principales errores que cometen los clubes cuando utilizan la inteligencia artificial? R: Hay una parte de seguridad en los datos, a veces las malas prácticas por no haberse formado pueden llevar a multas por no cumplir con la reglamentación de datos. También, puedes exponerte a lo que se llaman las alucinaciones, que es ese momento en el que la IA no encuentra un dato o está desactualizado y tú no eres capaz de saber que eso está mal. Aunque, es cierto que cada vez está más ajustada la realidad. Se trata más de un factor humano que en sí de la IA. P: ¿Cómo cree que un club debe, por ejemplo, acceder a una información en la inteligencia artificial que parece que es cierta, pero es errónea? ¿Cómo debe trabajar para evitar que aparezca esa información y utilizarla? R: Al final hay herramientas que te pueden ayudar en ese sentido. Por ejemplo, si utilizas ChatGPT, sabes que se está basando en un montón de información de internet que puede ser verdadera o falsa, y luego hay, por ejemplo, herramientas como NotebookLM que lo que hacen es únicamente basarse en la información que tú le das, con lo cual si tú le pasas un PDF, ya sea una tesis doctoral, un estudio científico u otra cosa, se trata de una información real, porque está basada en esos datos que ya has verificado o que se supone que son reales, con lo cual conocer estas herramientas y saber qué casos de uso conviene en cada momento es importante. P: Me gustaría preguntarle por el caso del Wolfsburgo que utiliza incluso hasta 100 inteligencias artificiales. ¿Qué nos puede enseñar ese caso para la gestión de ellas a los demás clubes? R: Este es un caso muy pionero que salió en Alemania, y al final lo que utilizábamos hasta hace un tiempo eran los llamados GPTs, que eran como pequeños asistentes, que estaban diseñados para una tarea concreta, con lo cual tú ahora tenías que hacer, por ejemplo, una rueda de prensa y le pedías que te la hiciera en base a tal información, y él tenía el contexto de todo lo que utilizaba. Al final podías acumular 100, 200 o incluso 300. Ahora se ha reorganizado, y dentro de un mismo proyecto puede tener varios temas, con lo cual puede ser entrenado en varias cosas, y no hace falta que sean como 100 distintos. P: ¿Cree que en algún momento todos los clubes profesionales van a utilizar de alguna forma u otra la inteligencia artificial? R: Yo creo que, todos los equipos de Primera División, internamente ya la están usando. Ahora, la pregunta es, ¿cuántos han sido formados? Yo sé que algunos sí, por ejemplo, el Deportivo de A Coruña a sus trabajadores, el Cádiz está haciendo cosas muy interesantes, no todos son de Primera. Hay clubes muy pequeños que están sabiendo aprovecharlas. P: ¿Qué trabajos dentro del fútbol cree que van a ser distintos en consecuencia de la inteligencia artificial en los próximos años y cuáles crees que realmente van a ser difícil de sustituir? R: Toda la parte de administración va a ser algo que va a cambiar radicalmente. Donde hoy hay cinco personas, en un futuro solo va a haber una. En la parte de comunicación y marketing va a cambiar para bien, las mismas personas que hoy están podrían hacer muchísimas más cosas. Entonces creemos que la evolución será allá donde se pueda crecer, es decir, donde haya una parte que mejorar, dónde podrán mantenerse esas personas, incluso ampliar. La cuestión es donde haya un trabajo que hacer y no se pueda hacer mucho más, pues ahí sí que se reducirá el tiempo y las horas empleadas radicalmente. P: ¿Cree realmente que la IA puede convertirse en una herramienta que los profesionales puedan ayudar para realmente facilitar y trabajar mejor en las funciones humanas como tal? R: Estoy absolutamente convencido. Esto es como el móvil, las redes sociales o internet, nadie se plantea hoy trabajar sin electricidad, sin un teléfono, sin un portátil o sin cualquier herramienta que hoy utilices de estas características. P: Si el día de mañana le llega un club profesional de fútbol o futsal y le pregunta cómo empezar a utilizar la IA, ¿cuál sería el primer consejo que le diría? R: Que se apunten a la newsletter gratuita que es pablosala.es, que hagan ese recorrido de recibir un correo cada día e ir aplicándolo, y cuando se queden estancados, después de un mes más o menos, que llegue ese momento en el que tienes un cierto dominio, pero que ya no puedes avanzar mucho más, entonces que me llamen.

articles.title: Anthony Gordon: "En Inglaterra nunca se me valoró realmente y en España sí aprecian mi inteligencia"
articles.standfirst: Anthony Gordon se mostró crítico con la visión que tenían de él en su país antes de fichar por el Barcelona
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon se mostró crítico con la visión que tenían de él en su país antes de fichar por el Barcelona
articles.body: Anthony Gordon, el delantero de 70 millones de euros del F.C. Barcelona que se confesó 'mourinhista', concedió una entrevista a 'ITV Sport' en la que considera que su talento "nunca fue plenamente respetado" en Inglaterra, motivo por el cual quiso marcharse de la Premier League. "Creo que me he convertido en un jugador diferente a los ojos de mucha gente, porque siempre sentí que en Inglaterra me respetaban por mi velocidad y mi presión, pero nunca llegaron a valorar realmente la calidad y la inteligencia con las que juego", destacó el ex del Newcastle. Gordon, que está protagonizando un gran inicio de temporada con el Barça de Hansi Flick, subrayó que "parece que sólo los compañeros con los que juego se dan cuenta de eso. Creo que ahora que estoy en el Barcelona y juego con un estilo diferente, esas cualidades resaltan mucho más y la gente empieza a percibir que no soy sólo rápido". El delantero de 25 años se mostró crítico con la visión que tenían de él en su país antes de fichar por el Barcelona: "Creo que en Inglaterra nunca se me valoró realmente, porque la gente sólo me veía como un jugador muy rápido y muy agresivo. En cambio, creo que en España sí aprecian mi inteligencia de juego y mi calidad; en el Barcelona, si no tienes buena técnica o inteligencia, desentonas muchísimo". "¿Si se me valora ahora más en Inglaterra? Creo que están empezando a hacerlo. Considero que aún hay margen de mejora en ese aspecto, pero ya están empezando a verlo al verme jugar en el Barcelona con un estilo futbolístico diferente, donde quizás esas otras cualidades resaltan más", apuntó. Gordon recordó que "jugué en el Newcastle, un equipo que basaba su juego en una gran intensidad y despliegue físico, por lo que lo que más destacaba era mi capacidad para correr y mi agresividad. Ahora practico un estilo totalmente opuesto, lo que permite que salgan a relucir mis otras cualidades". "Sí a veces es necesario irse para ser valorado y, sinceramente, eso era más o menos lo que yo quería. Quería dejar la Premier League. Buscaba una experiencia diferente y quería exactamente eso. Sentía que podía ofrecer más de lo que la gente pensaba de mí y quería demostrarlo en el escenario más importante del mundo", compartió.

articles.title: David Sánchez: "Lamine Yamal es el mejor jugador del mundo"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende en La Tribu que al azulgrana es "el mejor del mundo en la actualidad" y cree que su impacto más allá del fútbol puede jugar a su favor
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco defiende en La Tribu que al azulgrana es "el mejor del mundo en la actualidad" y cree que su impacto más allá del fútbol puede jugar a su favor
articles.body: El Balón de Oro entra en su recta final y David Sánchez tiene cada vez más claro hacia dónde puede decantarse el premio. El presentador de Despierta San Francisco analizó en La Tribu la carrera por el galardón y puso el foco especialmente en Lamine Yamal, al que ve con muchas opciones de terminar levantándolo. "Todo el mundo apunta a que las casas de apuestas señalan a Kane como gran favorito. Yo, a medida que adelantan y pasan los días, tengo la sensación de que lo va a ganar Lamine Yamal", aseguró David Sánchez. Para el periodista, las posibilidades del futbolista del Barcelona no se explican únicamente por su rendimiento sobre el terreno de juego. "Al margen de lo buen jugador que es, para mí el mejor del mundo en la actualidad, trasciende su imagen mucho más allá del fútbol", señaló. David Sánchez considera que esa dimensión también puede pesar en la elección: "Y eso no te penaliza y eso siempre suma. Igual que dicen que a Messi algún Balón de Oro lo ganó por todo lo que genera alrededor del fútbol, con Lamine Yamal empieza a pasar lo mismo". Por eso terminó lanzando un aviso de cara a la entrega del premio: "Para disgusto de los madridistas, no descarten ustedes que Lamine Yamal levante el día 26 su primer Balón de Oro". David Sánchez también habló del reconocimiento a los entrenadores, donde considera que el debate es mucho menor. "En la categoría de entrenador creo que no hay color. Creo que la justicia dice que Luis de la Fuente debería de levantar ese Balón de Oro", afirmó. El colaborador reconoció también los méritos de Luis Enrique: "Luis Enrique también hizo una gran temporada con el PSG, ganando la Liga y la Liga de Campeones", antes de insistir en su apuesta: "Está cantado que Luis de la Fuente, con todo el merecimiento del mundo, va a levantar ese Balón de Oro". Una situación que contrapuso a la batalla entre los futbolistas, cuyo debate considera ya demasiado prolongado: "El tema ya es agotador, es cansino y se nos está haciendo bastante largo por la campaña que se están marcando Mbappé y Lamine Yamal".

articles.title: Monchi pide perdón a la afición del Espanyol por darle el Balón de Oro a Lamine Yamal
articles.standfirst: Monchi justifica que apostó por Lamine Yamal "al tirar por la parte española", pero reconoce que como perico debería haber dicho cualquier otro"
articles.summary: Monchi justifica que apostó por Lamine Yamal "al tirar por la parte española", pero reconoce que como perico debería haber dicho cualquier otro"
articles.body: Monchi, director deportivo del R.C.D. Espanyol, pidió perdón en el programa 'El Larguero' por declarar que el barcelonista Lamine Yamal se merecía ganar el Balón de Oro: "Me han dicho entre Mbappé, francés, Harry Kane, inglés o Lamine Yamal, español, y he tirado por la parte española". "He generado un poco de polémica entre los aficionados pericos", reconoció en la cadena SER. "Si a alguien le ha molestado, pido disculpas", insistió Ramón Rodríguez Verdejo (Monchi) sobre sus declaraciones durante la presentación de la V edición de la Reyes Cup. Monchi explicó cuando le preguntaron por los candidatos a ganar el Balón de Oro él apostó por Lamine Yamal "al tirar por la parte española, pero como perico debería haber dicho cualquier otro". "Sé lo que es el sentimiento perico, pero he dicho a Lamine Yamal poniéndome la bandera española", apuntó. Monchi valoró en 'El Larguero' el inicio de temporada del Espanyol, que suma 7 puntos de 21 posibles y lleva dos derrotas seguidas. "Me ha sorprendido mucho para bien lo exigente que es la afición del Espanyol. Crecer al lado de un equipo tan imponente como el Barcelona te hace sentir tu identidad mucho más... Hay necesidad en el ambiente de que sea una temporada tranquila y ojalá seamos capaces de retomar el camino", compartió. Monchi quiso destacar que ha ido "muy de la mano" con el entrenador Manolo González en la planificación deportiva: "Entre cuerpo técnico y dirección deportiva hemos decidido los nombres. Veremos si hemos acertado cuando termine la temporada, pero, al menos, hemos ido de la mano". "El momento más importante de la planificación es cuando eres capaz de interpretar el perfil de jugador que necesita el entrenador. Soy de los que piensa que los entrenadores no tienen que decidir los nombres, sino los perfiles", explicó. Sobre el mediático fichaje de Bryan Zaragoza reconoció que "Fue complicada la operación en sí, pero fue fácil convencer al chico. Él tenía ganas de volver a España, que es su hábitat natural, dónde mejor rinde. La combinación con Manolo fue muy positiva. Llegó con un déficit físico importante, pero poco a poco estamos viendo al Bryan que queremos".

articles.summary: Aston Villa's summer signing Johan Manzambi has been nominated for the best young player at the Ballon d'Or ceremony. BBC Sport looks at his rise.
articles.body:
In just two years Johan Manzambi has gone from being an unknown teenager to a European star.

The 20-year-old could be named young talent of the year at the Ballon d'Or ceremony next month having only made his senior debut for Freiburg in 2024.

A breakout season in Germany last term convinced Villa to pay more than £50m for a player with just 47 club starts.

Manzambi scored on his full Villa debut to help secure a first Premier League win of the season and now faces Scotland with Switzerland in the Nations League on Tuesday looking to continue his progression.

Vega hails Yakin and Manzambi as Swiss head for Hampden

Villa complete club record Manzambi signing

Manzambi is already in the discussion with fellow nominees Lamine Yamal of Barcelona, Real Madrid's Yan Diomande and new Manchester City midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi for the best young player in the world award.

He scored three goals in four games for Switzerland at the World Cup before a knee injury ended his tournament, only a year after making his full international debut.

It is a rapid rise for a player who used to return to Freiburg's academy to do his washing.

Bernhard Weis, who gave Manzambi his debut for Freiburg Under-19s, told BBC Sport: "He is playing for the professionals and he comes to us at the academy and brings some dirty clothes.

"He didn't have a washing machine so he comes here and washes some clothes.

"I would speak with him and then he would pick up some young guys from the under-13s, under-14s and take them to the train station.

"He would see the guys and say, 'come with me, I'll take you to the station', so they could get home. That's Johan Manzambi."

As for his profile, though, Weis did not expect a Ballon d'Or nomination coming so quickly.

He added: "I didn't see that. I saw something for the first team, for us, but this way, no chance.

"The first half year at Freiburg it was not so easy for him, he's not so strong and he's not so stable. He put on five kilos and then he thought, 'now I go, it's the right moment, I will be faster and stronger'.

Massimo Lombardo, Servette's academy director agreed. He first worked with Manzambi when he was 15 and oversaw his early development before he moved to Freiburg as a 17-year-old in 2023.

"It is a real surprise for many people, that he can do something special so quickly," he told BBC Sport.

"For me, the difference he can make is because of his mentality, personality, enthusiasm and courage. He has the technical skills and tactical skills and the physical possibility now to perform in England.

Why Newcastle target Manzambi is in demand

"Mentally he was always a player who, when he came into the training session and games, always wanted to do something important. You can see that as a player who starts with Freiburg, he took his chance.

"I can remember his second game with Switzerland, against the USA and he scored. It was always important for him to come into the game and to do something."

Last season Manzambi was named the Europa League's Young Player of the Season, as Freiburg lost the final to Villa in May .

He scored 12 goals in 61 appearances and Weis, now Freiburg II boss, has watched him develop, with Manzambi also learning German in three months.

It helped him swiftly move from the academy to the first team, making his debut against Heidenheim a year after joining.

Weis described him a "difference maker" and, among players in the Bundesliga in his position last season, Manzambi ranked first for 10-plus metre progressive carries (116), shot-ending carries (13) and fouls won (78).

Villa knew he would move this summer so it was a case of now or never for Emery. Had he gone to Newcastle instead they believed his next move would put him out of their financial reach.

The Magpies were always wary of being hijacked, having previously lost Victor Munoz to Liverpool and, while they agreed a deal with Freiburg, they never got a yes from Manzambi.

Villa then turned the versatile forward into the most expensive Swiss player in history - surpassing Granit Xhaka's £38.25m move from Borussia Mönchengladbach to Arsenal 10 years ago.

Yet, despite signing a five-year deal, Weis backed him to make the next step quickly.

"I think Aston Villa is the right club for him. He will play every time when he is fit and that's the right way. Then I think he plays two seasons at Villa and then he goes to the next step," he added.

"After the World Cup I said he must go to the Premier League. Bayern Munich were mentioned, he didn't go to [Borussia] Dortmund, [Bayer] Leverkusen. It's the right way."

'A young player who wanted to do something special'

Freiburg have made light of Manzambi's absence and went into the international break unbeaten and sitting third, having topped the Bundesliga after three straight opening wins.

Without him they have won six of their seven games in all competitions, scoring 24 goals, and boss Julian Schuster said earlier this month he had hoped to keep the player.

It was the same for Lombardo at Servette, who fought to keep their young talent, but the former Switzerland international admitted Manzambi had made the right decisions.

"We wanted him to stay with us, we gave him a contract but he wouldn't sign and history would say it's a good way, he came to Freiburg and played with the under-19s and was always improving," said the ex-Perugia midfielder.

"Then Johan came into the first team and performed so well he started to play from the beginning and the coach couldn't move him from the starting XI.

"With us he was incredible, he wanted to stay on the pitch to improve, to stay in the games and he had a lot of personality at 15. You can see into a group of young players who has the personality to speak.

"He has a lot of personality. Other players were stronger and quicker but he trained with enthusiasm and I saw a young player who wanted to do something special."

articles.title: Beitia y Marchal, los otros 'fichajes'
articles.standfirst: El central y el extremo, puestos en los que había quienes pedían más incorporaciones, son los dos futbolistas del Sanse que han contado en la Real en el primer tramo de curso
articles.summary: El central y el extremo, puestos en los que había quienes pedían más incorporaciones, son los dos futbolistas del Sanse que han contado en la Real en el primer tramo de curso
articles.body: Luken Beitia y Álex Marchal son los dos futbolistas del Sanse que han tenido minutos con la Real Sociedad en el primer tramo de campeonato, en el que el primero ha disputado como titular y completos cuatro de los ocho encuentros, participando el segundo en el mismo número de choques, pero saliendo siempre desde el banquillo. Parecía que otros compañeros suyos en el segundo equipo como Gorka Carrera o Ibai Aguirre podían contar algo para Pellegrino Matarazzo, pero no ha sido así. Marchal fue el primer futbolista del Sanse en tener minutos con la Real, dentro de esa apuesta por la cantera que el presidente Jokin Aperribay y el director de fútbol Erik Bretos aseguraron que iba a haber esta temporada, al salir el extremo, que ya había contado bastante para Matarazzo en la pretemporada, a falta de media hora para el final del primer partido oficial, en La Cartuja ante el Betis. Otro de los que había tenido protagonismo en la preparación fue Beitia, que se convirtió en una de las dos grande sorpresas del técnico de Nueva Jersey en la alineación inicial que presentó en la visita al Real Madrid en el Santiago Bernabéu, junto a la del recién ascendido a la Real Job Ochieng. Marchal contó luego también minutos en las rectas finales de los encuentros frente a Espanyol, Celta y Elche, dejando luego de tener protagonismo al realizar en el Martínez Valero una gran actuación Ochieng, precisamente el jugador que ya el año pasado en el Sanse le relegó al banquillo. El relevo en cuanto a la presencia de futbolistas del segundo equipo en el primero lo cogió Beitia, que después de tres partidos sin pisar el verde volvió al once ante el Atlético y se ha mantenido en el contra Bournemouth y Valencia, con buenas actuaciones además. Había aficionados que, además de Mamadou Sarr, pedían fichar otro central y el de Elgoibar ha demostrado que puede ser él. También estaban los que deseaban una cara nueva en ataque y Marchal es la que han visto.

articles.title: FIFA could disburse millions to members as Infantino seeks re-election
articles.summary: FIFA president Infantino is open to providing ‘greatest level of additional funding’ to associations amid opposition.
articles.body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is willing ‌‌‌‌to discuss the disbursement of millions of dollars to ⁠⁠⁠⁠the member associations of football’s global governing body as the Swiss chief seeks re-election to the post he has held for 10 years amid growing opposition.

The ⁠⁠⁠⁠amount of the distributions to individual nations will be on the agenda of the FIFA Council’s October 15 meeting, according to a ⁠⁠⁠⁠letter Infantino sent to the heads of the six regional confederations, as reported by media in the United States on Monday.

“I will not prejudge the amount,” Infantino wrote, according ⁠⁠⁠⁠to one report. “I will support the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered through FIFA’s proper governance process, applied fairly and supported by transparent and auditable arrangements. The ambition is welcome. The financial evidence, governance and implementation must now support ‌‌‌‌it.”

“A single figure can begin the discussion, but it cannot complete a global policy. I have therefore instructed the Secretary General to consolidate all submissions into one integrated assessment for consideration by the FIFA Council.”

The move is seen as Infantino’s latest attempt to placate regional football bodies, as well as their chiefs, in a bid to hold on to his position as the most powerful man in football.

Earlier this month, the 56-year-old confirmed his bid amid widespread criticism of his leadership and the growing threat of legal proceedings.

Infantino has faced stiff opposition since the fallout from his proposed plan to sell approximately 20 percent of a proposed new entity, FIFA ⁠⁠⁠⁠Forward Enterprise (FFE), focused on the commercial and operational facets of the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments.

The Swiss-Italian has been the most powerful man in world football over the past 10 years, but has increasingly lost support from regional football confederations and national associations. Last month, he appeared to be pulling out all the stops in a bid to retain his position, despite growing calls for his ousting and wide-ranging disapproval of his plans.

On Friday, the English Premier League and three other top European leagues called for governance reform of FIFA .

A joint statement with leagues from Spain, Italy and Germany accused Infantino of actively promoting “exploitative ideas rather than safeguarding against them”.

He is seen as a divisive figure in international football , with his close ties to some of the most powerful global leaders and plans for maximising revenue from football viewed as a threat to the game.

With fewer than six months until the next round of elections for FIFA’s presidency, Infantino appears to be losing ground among his usual backers.

FIFA presidents are limited to three terms, each lasting four years.

However, in 2022, Infantino successfully argued that his first spell in charge, which began when he was elected at an extraordinary FIFA Congress in 2016 following Sepp Blatter’s resignation, should not count towards that limit because it completed an interrupted mandate.

His plans to run for a fourth term have been questioned by critics and rights groups, who have asked FIFA’s Governance, Audit and Compliance Committee (GACC) to block the re-election bid.

The financial discussion comes in the wake of UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC calling for Infantino to resign over the plan.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF’s Victor Montagliani recently wrote a letter to FIFA, seeking payments such as the one Infantino addressed in his letter. Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, head ⁠⁠⁠⁠of the Asian Football Confederation, made a similar request, per the reports.

Among the investors ⁠⁠⁠⁠in FFE was to be Joshua Kushner, the ⁠⁠⁠⁠brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner. Trump is a close ally of Infantino.

Infantino subsequently abandoned the private equity plan, but he has refused to resign, and he plans to run for re-election ‌‌‌‌in March. With seven weeks remaining for candidates to announce their intention to oppose Infantino, no challenger has stepped forward.

Had Infantino’s FFE plan gone through, each ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌member ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌nation would have received at least $20m. The letter from UEFA and CONCACAF asks for every member association to receive a minimum of $10m from FIFA’s reserves, according to the reports.

articles.title: 30 años del "Rafa, no me jodas", la frase que nunca existió
articles.standfirst: Un erróneo "penalti y expulsión" lanzó a la fama al juez de línea Rafa Guerrero
articles.summary: Un erróneo "penalti y expulsión" lanzó a la fama al juez de línea Rafa Guerrero
articles.body: Aquel 29 de septiembre de 1996, La Romareda fue escenario de una de esas escenas arbitrales que terminan adquiriendo vida propia. El Barcelona había generado una acción a balón parado que terminó sin consecuencias para los visitantes, pero el verdadero conflicto llegó después, dentro del área. Couto golpeó a Aguado y Solana reaccionó propinando un manotazo en la cabeza al jugador portugués, que exageró la caída y terminó por el suelo. El asistente que por entonces apenas empezaba a hacerse conocido, Rafa Guerrero, llamó a Mejuto González hacia la banda para explicarle lo que acababa de presenciar. Su conclusión fue contundente: "Penalti y expulsión". A partir de ahí nació una de las frases más célebres de la historia reciente del arbitraje español. La televisión captó la respuesta de Mejuto y aquella reacción se convirtió inmediatamente en protagonista. Mucho antes de que existieran las redes sociales y los hashtags, "¡Rafa no me jodas!" se instaló en el imaginario colectivo. Pero la frase que pasó a la historia no fue exactamente la que pronunció el árbitro. La grabación permite comprobar que sus palabras fueron otras: "Venga, joder Rafa, me cago en mi madre, ¿expulsión de quién?". Con el paso del tiempo, la expresión terminó reducida a ese popular 'Rafanomejodas', aunque la versión literal era distinta. Guerrero, mientras tanto, no dudó de su interpretación de la jugada. Insistió en que había visto claramente la infracción: ("el balón estaba en juego y es penalti"). Tras varias conversaciones entre ambos, tres en total, Mejuto terminó señalando la pena máxima. El problema llegó con la tarjeta: Aguado, identificado por el asistente como ("el número 6"), fue quien acabó expulsado, aunque la decisión correcta habría correspondido a Solana.

articles.title: Liverpool: Inside the club's increasing global investment in youth
articles.summary: Liverpool are becoming increasingly proactive in their search for global young talent. BBC Sport takes a closer look.
articles.body:
Liverpool may have made three signings worth more than £100m each over the past two summers in Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola, but internally there is a realisation that after a significant amount of young talent was sold last summer, the club need to replenish that talent pool.

Since 2020, Liverpool have made more than £230m from selling players who have represented them at youth level and that has been a major part of owner Fenway Sports Group's self-sustaining business model, with the funds reinvested into the club.

Since Brexit, there is a 'premium' on young English players and it is why Liverpool 's global talent department, led by Matt Newberry since the winter of 2024, now have a major role to play.

Fifa rules state that international transfers of players are only permitted if the player is over 18 and, since Brexit, Premier League clubs are no longer permitted to sign players under 18 from European countries.

Newberry's team is responsible for deciding which young talents from overseas should be targeted for a move. Using their wealth of contacts across the world, including dedicated regional scouts, Liverpool are becoming increasingly aggressive in the space.

It helps that new sporting director Julian Ward is well known for his global network.

"Any player we sign, the first intention is that we want them to play in the first team and there's a belief that there's a chance for everyone that signs here," Alex Inglethorpe, Liverpool Academy director told BBC Sport.

"That really is no different since the impact of Brexit on the English market, which is quite significant. There's now a premium on young English players. Time will tell if that premium is worthwhile but it's definitely a change.

"So it's fairly natural for a club like Liverpool to look within Merseyside in the first instance then broaden that out - national recruitment happens at 14 and after that you look globally, which is what we've done."

Ndiaye's 'incredible story' from Senegal to Anfield

Mor Talla Ndiaye's journey began in the Senegalese village of Sandiara where he played football in the streets.

He progressed through the ranks playing for Bousports Academy in the town of Thiadiaye before joining Amitie Football Club in the city of Thies.

Come January this year, Liverpool fended off interest from other European clubs and signed the 18-year-old for about £1m plus add-ons.

"You have access to certain talent based on points accrued from playing homegrown players. We had a couple of ESC (elite significant contribution) spots to explore the wider market and that's something which, even prior to Brexit, was a fairly normal thing," Inglethorpe adds.

Ndiaye is a left-footed centre-half who played for Liverpool in pre-season under Andoni Iraola and was an unused substitute in three games in the second half of last season under Arne Slot.

"He's an incredible story, isn't he? From where he's come from to where he is - and he's such a humble kid. He's an unbelievable lad to work with," Rob Page, Liverpool 's U21 boss, told BBC Sport.

"There's exciting times ahead but he's got a lot of work to do. He's nowhere near the finished article but he's on the right path. His attitude is spot on and he's at the club that will definitely help him develop."

At Liverpool , there is an optimism regarding Ndiaye and a genuine belief that if he makes it to the top, it could be one of the great football stories.

Liverpool opened discussions with his academy and his agency, Sport Cover, after scouts spotted his performances at the U17 World Cup in Qatar last winter and several video calls were arranged before the club's representatives travelled to Senegal.

Once there, they visited where Ndiaye trained, as well as meeting the people that supported his development before presenting their vision to him directly.

A round-table meeting was organised with his family to help understand his environment, the story and the context in which he grew up.

Ultimately, Ndiaye chose Liverpool because they offered the clearest pathway and their approach in getting to know him stood out.

Ndukwe, Martinez, Brughmans and others to watch

Ndiaye isn't the only player to have been identified and recruited by Liverpool 's global talent team.

After the U17 World Cup, Liverpool also made a £2.6m move for another centre-half, Ifeanyi Ndukwe.

Ndukwe was impressive in pre-season and the 18-year-old Austrian has gone on loan to Levante in La Liga as he looks to obtain a UK work permit.

The list doesn't stop there. Samuel Martinez, the 17-year-old Colombian midfielder, will join next summer after having " 30 offers from around the world , external ", according to his father.

It doesn't always work. Arsenal beat Liverpool to the signing of Andria Bartishvili from Georgia last month and the 17-year-old will join the Gunners next summer when he is 18.

But the moves for Martinez and Ndiaye showcase Liverpool 's willingness to spread beyond Europe and into areas they may not have explored before. Given the inevitability of other top clubs circling emerging talent, the idea of selling the pathway that Liverpool offers is imperative.

Since arriving, Ndiaye has settled in with a host family - which is normal when players aren't from the area - that are used to working with Liverpool .

"Players come from varying parts of the world and, when someone comes in and doesn't speak much English at the start, you have to help with that and help understand culturally the differences in food, the weather and even the pitches you play on," Inglethorpe said.

"There's a lot of understanding in terms of the level of support that's needed and the most important thing you can give a young player is the time.

"I'm delighted that Mor made such a strong impression and he's done as well as he has, but we hope that he's going to get better and better as he continues to adapt."

This summer, Liverpool also confirmed moves for Lucca Brughmans, the 18-year-old Belgian goalkeeper, and Djylian N'Guessan, the 18-year-old French forward, with both set to join the club permanently in 2027.

In the modern game, most talents are known and there aren't many hidden gems anymore, but Liverpool believe that by digging deeper and wider they can get ahead of the curve, using their global network and their reputation as a club that will help players develop.

articles.title: Fifa accuses Uefa of 'misinformation campaign'
articles.summary: Uefa's suggestions that Fifa president Gianni Infantino "violated any law or ethical principle are categorically without merit" says world football's governing body.
articles.body:
Fifa has accused Uefa of a "misinformation campaign" and attempting to influence the race for its presidential campaign in new court documents.

Last month European football's governing body filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

Uefa accused Fifa president Gianni Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" and "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by [him] for his own benefit" over the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

In its response on Monday night, world governing body Fifa said Uefa's filing contained "numerous false or misleading statements about Fifa and Infantino".

"With no basis whatsoever, Uefa suggests that Mr Infantino sought to profit personally from the FFE proposal," Fifa said in a filing in the Southern District of Florida, opposing Uefa's motion for discovery.

"Uefa's suggestions that Mr Infantino violated any law or ethical principle are categorically without merit."

It also described Uefa's filing as "farcically overbroad" saying "districts faced with similar requests have outright rejected such applications".

BBC Sport has contacted Uefa for comment. BBC Sport has been told insiders believe that if Fifa has nothing to hide, it should disclose the documents and speed up the legal process.

Uefa has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down from three confederations.

Fifa's FFE plan proposed selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, sparking a major backlash.

Infantino faced calls for his resignation but claimed the project had been intended to generate additional money for the game.

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan, and called for an independent review of FFE.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

articles.title: What Florida coach Jon Sumrall said about Missouri football before top-10 visit
articles.summary: Here’s what new Florida coach Jon Sumrall said about Missouri football before the top-10 Gators’ visit to Columbia on Saturday.
articles.body:
If Missouri is going to bounce back from its first loss of the year, a top-10 team and a new, still-undefeated head coach stand in the Tigers ' way.

Mizzou football faces undefeated Florida this coming Saturday, Oct. 3 at Memorial Stadium. The Gators , who hired Jon Sumrall from Tulane in the offseason to replace Billy Napier, are on a four-game winning streak to start Sumrall's tenure, including a 52-28 win over Ole Miss this past Saturday that catapulted Florida to the No. 8 ranking in the nation.

The Tigers (3-1, 0-1 SEC) lost to Mississippi State 31-24 in Week 4. Drinkwitz has won both games he's coached against Florida in Columbia, but this looks like a different challenge.

During his weekly press conference Monday in Gainesville, here's what Sumrall said about Missouri ahead of the Gators' visit to Columbia.

On QB Austin Simmons , a one-time Florida commit

Simmons, who is from Miami, lost for the first time as Mizzou's starting quarterback on Saturday, but he made some crucial plays and big throws across the second and third quarters to get Mizzou out of a 14-point hole and give the Tigers the lead going into the final 15 minutes.

Before reclassifying from the Class of 2025 to the 2023 class and flipping to Ole Miss, Simmons was once committed to Florida.

"I've always heard he's really highly intelligent," Sumrall said about Simmons. "He graduated high school young and college super fast. Like, intelligent guy, number one. Big arm, can make all the throws. Good athlete. Yeah, I mean he was the starter a year ago at the last place (Ole Miss) for a reason until he got hurt, and then Drink wouldn't have brought him in if he … hadn't seen enough of him to know he could be an SEC-winning quarterback.

"The guy's got all the physical tools, too. So, I've got a lot of respect for what the kid can be. He's talented."

Sumrall on Mizzou O-Line: 'Best offensive line we've played'

Sumrall had a viral soundbite ahead of the Gators' game against Ole Miss when he was told Florida was the betting favorite over the then-top 10 Rebels. His response: "Who has us favored against these guys? There's a lot of good drugs out there (in Las Vegas), huh?"

He had a tag for that punchline, referencing his time as the head coach at Troy, where he tried to recruit current starting Mizzou right guard Curtis Peagler , who was an in-state recruit from Demopolis, Alabama.

"I mentioned last week that Vegas was on drugs," Sumrall said. "I don't know what I was doing at the time. I thought I had a chance to get this kid at Troy."

Through four games so far this season, Mizzou has the best pass-blocking grade in the country at Pro Football Focus. The Tigers have only allowed 11 pressures on the quarterback, which is the fewest in the SEC.

"It starts up front with them. You look at the offensive line, I think this is the best offensive line we've played. Their left tackle ( Cayden Green ) is a big-time player. … Their O-line is really good."

Sumrall said that Drinkwitz texted him before his press conference telling him, "not to talk about our first interaction," which seemingly came while the two coaches were recruiting the Mobile, Alabama, area while Sumrall was an assistant Tulane and Drinkwitz was an assistant at Arkansas State.

"He's a guy that (I've) always had a good relationship with," Sumrall said.

That means they go back at least 13 years, which means Sumrall — a former defensive assistant — has some familiarity with what Drinkwitz's offenses look like.

"You can still see Drink's influence and what their identity is," Sumrall said. "They're as good of an outside zone running team as anybody in college football. … I think they play the game the way it's meant to be played. A lot of respect for how they play the game, and we've got our work cut out for us to win up front this week."

Don't expect to see Jon Sumrall in downtown Columbia for the homecoming parade on Saturday morning.

He was asked about facing Mizzou in its homecoming game, and whether or not he can use that as a source of motivation for his team.

"I have zero concerns about anybody's homecoming. Our homecoming. I just — it's a football game," Sumrall said. "I do know this, the last four trips we've gone to Missouri, we've lost three of them. So, if we think it's going to be a freaking cakewalk, I don't care if it's homecoming or whatever, we're in for a rude awakening. And, so, we've got to get ready to play a really good football team on the road in a place that's not gone well for us a lot recently — in the most recent history.

"So, I'm really worried about that. I don't care who their homecoming king or queen (is) or any of that."

articles.title: Latest injury update for Army football running back Godspower Nwawuihe
articles.summary: Army running back Godspower Nwawuihe was injured in the Temple contest. Here's the latest on his recovery.
articles.body:
It's going to be wait-and-see time for the recovery of injured Army running back Godspower Nwawuihe .

The sophomore was injured early in the third quarter of Friday's 21-17 victory at Temple . On Army's second offensive series of the half, Nwawuihe was mauled at the line of scrimmage by Temple's Russell Sykes IV for a 1-yard gain on first down and then got the next handoff to the left side, falling forward awkwardly for a 3-yard gain. He left the game and was taken to the locker room.

The next time he appeared, he was on the Army sidelines without his pads. In his absence, Jake Rendina and Carson Smith picked up more of the running duties as Army rallied for the victory.

Nwawuihe did not work out on Sunday, said Army head coach Jeff Monken on his Monday night radio show, "This Week in Army Football ."

"We're going to wait and see,'' Monken said. "He was hurt pretty bad. He was in a sling ... on Friday night. Our trainers have started the rehabilitation process — we've got a great medical staff here and they're taking good care of him.

"It's probably going to be a few days, maybe longer, to figure out just exactly what's going on with it, and when you have an injury like that, oftentimes it takes a little bit more time. I'm confident that if he can come back and play he will. He's a tough kid and he's got great care, so time will tell.''

The absence of Nwawuihe puts a crimp in Army's rushing attack, although the Black Knights have done well moving the ball with Rendina (13 carries, 56 yards), Smith (16 carries, 80 yards) and running threat Cale Hellums (47 carries, 246 yards) at quarterback. Nwawuihe has 37 carries for 164 yards.

Monken said Smith's inspired performance in the comeback effort will certainly help. Smith had six carries for 35 yards, gaining three first downs on the decisive winning drive.

"It was just a matter of both of those guys (Smith and Rendina) getting a chance to touch the ball and get the carries,'' Monken said. "I think once we started handing it to Carson, you could see there's just a difference. He was gaining those tough yards, and every time he had it, it was 6, 7, 12 yards. At that point, give it to the guy with the hot hand.''

Army travels to Ruston, Louisiana, to take on Louisiana Tech in a non-conference game at 7:30 p.m. Saturday, October 3. The same clubs met in the 2024 Independence Bowl , with Army prevailing 27-6.

articles.title: Liverpool defender Jacquet shines on France debut but vows to raise his game: “I can do much better”
articles.summary: Jeremy Jacquet has said he can still get better despite an impressive senior debut for France against Belgium.Jacquet made his first appearance for the natio...
articles.body:
Jeremy Jacquet has said he can still get better despite an impressive senior debut for France against Belgium .

Jacquet made his first appearance for the national team during the 1-0 win over Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on Monday night.

The Liverpool defender was included in the France squad for the first time this month, following an eye-catching adaptation to the Premier League.

The 21-year-old helped France to a clean sheet on debut, and led his teammates for tackles (4) in an accomplished performance. Jacquet also won 6/9 defensive duels, completed 91.8% of his passes, and had the joint-most passes into the final third (10).

"I'm keeping my feet on the ground" – Jeremy Jacquet shines on France debut but vows to improve after Belgium win

Despite a strong showing on debut for Les Bleus , Jacquet insisted he was not satisfied and outlined his desire to improve.

"Am I satisfied with my performance? No," he told TF1.

"I'm thinking about two or three times in the attacking phase when I could have done much better with my passing.

"I'm not going to get into whether I'll become a starter. I'm taking my time and keeping my feet on the ground.

"I'm asked to play, I'm given instructions and I try to follow them. I've got my head screwed on."

articles.title: ‘About time…’ Mike Tomlin breaking unwritten rules of coaching with Dallas Cowboys comments
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin’s recent venture into football analysis has gotten off to a somewhat controversial start, after the former Pittsburgh Steelers’ head coach questi...
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin's recent venture into football analysis has gotten off to a somewhat controversial start, after the former Pittsburgh Steelers ' head coach questioned the Dallas Cowboys .

Tomlin was replaced, ironically, by former Dallas Cowboys head coach Mike McCarthy as the head coach for the Steelers this spring.

Perhaps that is what motivated him to break what some consider to be an unspoken code of conduct within the coaching fraternity.

Mike Tomlin's criticism of Dallas Cowboys coaching comes as 'refreshing' change to NFL analysis

Speaking during NBC's Sunday Night Football coverage, Mike Tomlin did something almost no head coach-turned-analyst has done – criticise the Dallas Cowboys coaching staff.

While Tomlin never mentioned HC Brian Schottenheimer and DC Christian Parker, he did question the negligent defensive scheme they drew up that allowed the Baltimore Ravens to steal the walk-off win.

"I thought the sequence played by the Dallas Cowboys at the end of the game was somewhat negligent, to be quite honest with you.

"It was seven seconds left to go in regulation; they kick a touchback. Baltimore gets the ball on the 35-yard-line. They had this really significant play down the middle of the field down to their number one receiver, Zay Flowers…

"I'm really surprised they're playing man-to-man in this sequence… It put them in position to make that game-winning field goal… Strategically, Dallas helped them in that circumstance."

As mentioned before, almost no former head coach who became a TV analyst has ever criticised the coaching staff for their decisions in such a manner.

Some schemes and plays are certainly debated, but former coaches usually treat their kind like a fraternity, choosing not to bring down their fellow coaches after a mistake of any kind.

Former ESPN editor Chuck Salituro praised Tomlin for his approach to broadcast analysis, telling Front Office Sports that he is making himself a valuable addition to NBC's coverage team.

"It's refreshing, accurate, completely fair, professional, and about time. The hardest thing in my experience for former coaches and players is to separate themselves from the brethren and tell us how they really feel, especially in their first year of TV work.

"I always told new analysts you no longer work for the team or the league and with the coaches and players. You work for our audience.

"The audience has to come before any past allegiances. You owe your best work and professional honesty to the audience first."

How Tomlin's comments will go down with the larger active and inactive NFL coaching community remains a mystery.

But it's hard to imagine them being happy, especially considering the unspoken precedent previous coaches-turned-broadcasters had set.

articles.title: Real Madrid, Barcelona and Liverpool still tracking Dortmund star
articles.summary: Nico Schlotterbeck was heavily linked with a move away from Borussia Dortmund earlier this year.He eventually signed a new contract with BVB until 2031, but...
articles.body:
Nico Schlotterbeck was heavily linked with a move away from Borussia Dortmund earlier this year.

He eventually signed a new contract with BVB until 2031, but that did little to end the speculation, with reports revealing that the deal included a clause allowing him to leave for a select group of clubs for €50-60 million during the summer transfer window.

However, when Schlotterbeck suffered a rather serious ankle injury during Germany's second World Cup game against Côte d'Ivoire, it became clear that a quick departure from BVB wouldn't happen.

The 26-year-old made his return to action against Paderborn on September 12, and now that the defender is fully fit again, speculation surrounding his future has been reignited.

According to transfer insider Ekrem Konur, Liverpool , Real Madrid and Barcelona continue to monitor Schlotterbeck, with the three clubs reportedly seeing him as a potential long-term option at the back.

German media have suggested that the centre-back's release clause will become active again in summer 2027, so speculation over his future will likely intensify as the season progresses.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA accuses European football chiefs of 'harassment' against world governing body's president
articles.summary: FIFA has accused UEFA of a "misinformation campaign" and attempting to influence the race for its presidential campaign; FIFA president Gianni Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until Nov 18 to find an alternative candidate
articles.body:
The claims are made in a court filing in Miami by FIFA, which has been obtained by Sky News , seeking to block UEFA's request for all the evidence related to the attempt to sell shares in the World Cup to private investors , also known as the FIFA Forward Enterprise [FFE] proposal

FIFA's lawyers write: "UEFA's conduct demonstrates that its application was made in bad faith and for the purpose of harassment."

UEFA has sought all documents on the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme, saying it could pursue a case against Mr Infantino for criminal mismanagement, alleging he undersold the tournaments for personal financial benefit.

But FIFA's lawyers write: "With no basis whatsoever, UEFA suggests that Mr Infantino sought to profit personally from the FFE proposal."

The crisis has erupted ahead of Mr Infantino's bid for re-election in March 2027 with UEFA withdrawing its support but not yet proposing a rival candidate ahead of the deadline in November.

FIFA's legal submission says: "Just before FIFA's election, UEFA filed this application [and three others] spreading misinformation regarding Mr Infantino. This court should reject any attempt to influence FIFA's presidential election based on these grounds."

UEFA has said it has lost confidence in Infantino despite the abandonment of FFE and is seeking to put forward a credible alternative candidate to challenge him in next year's presidential election.

FIFA's filing questions the timing of UEFA's legal application, pointing out that the deadline for submitting candidates is November 18.

"This court should reject any attempt to influence FIFA's presidential election based on these grounds," the filings state.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with opponents now seeking to find an alternative candidate.
